name: Block
author: John Conway
description: The smallest and most common 4-cell still life in Conway's Game of Life.

name: Bee-hive
author: John Conway
description: A common 6-cell hexagonal still life frequently produced from random soups.

name: Loaf
author: John Conway
description: A 7-cell still life resembling a loaf of bread, the third most common still life.

name: Boat
author: John Conway
description: The only 5-cell still life in Conway's Game of Life.

name: Tub
author: John Conway
description: A symmetric 4-cell still life forming a hollow diamond shape.

name: Ship
author: John Conway
description: A 6-cell still life closely related to the boat with an extra corner cell.

name: Pond
author: John Conway
description: An 8-cell still life with fourfold rotational symmetry.

name: Eater 1
author: Bill Gosper
description: A 7-cell still life capable of absorbing gliders and other small patterns without permanent damage.

name: Blinker
author: John Conway
description: The smallest and most common oscillator, alternating between a horizontal and vertical line of three cells.

name: Toad
author: Simon Norton
description: A compact 6-cell period-2 oscillator discovered in 1970.

name: Beacon
author: John Conway
description: A period-2 oscillator consisting of two diagonally touching blocks that repeatedly flash.

name: Clock
author: Simon Norton
description: A 6-cell period-2 oscillator whose two central cells rotate back and forth like clock hands.

name: Pulsar
author: John Conway
description: The most common period-3 oscillator, featuring fourfold symmetry and 48 initial cells.

name: Octagon 2
author: Sol Goodman & Arthur Taber
description: The first known period-5 oscillator, discovered independently in 1971.

name: Figure Eight
author: Simon Norton
description: A period-8 oscillator formed by two 3x3 blocks placed diagonally corner-to-corner.

name: Kok's Galaxy
author: Jan Kok
description: A classic period-8 pinwheel oscillator discovered in 1971 and used as Golly's icon.

name: Penta-decathlon
author: John Conway
description: A period-15 oscillator that evolves from a single 10-cell row and is widely used as a glider reflector.

name: Queen Bee Shuttle
author: Bill Gosper
description: A period-30 shuttle oscillator where a queen bee bounces between two stabilizing blocks.

name: Twin Bees Shuttle
author: Bill Gosper
description: A period-46 oscillator with two mirrored queen bees bouncing between stabilizing blocks.

name: Glider
author: Richard Guy
description: The smallest and most famous diagonal spaceship, traveling at c/4.

name: Lightweight Spaceship (LWSS)
author: John Conway
description: The smallest orthogonal spaceship, moving horizontally at c/2.

name: Middleweight Spaceship (MWSS)
author: John Conway
description: An 11-cell orthogonal c/2 spaceship slightly larger than the LWSS.

name: Heavyweight Spaceship (HWSS)
author: John Conway
description: A 13-cell orthogonal c/2 spaceship, the largest of the standard Conway spaceships.

name: Loafer
author: Josh Ball
description: A small 21-cell orthogonal spaceship traveling at c/7 discovered in 2013.

name: Copperhead
author: zdr
description: A symmetric 28-cell orthogonal c/10 spaceship discovered in 2016.

name: Coe Ship
author: Tim Coe
description: A 28-cell orthogonal c/2 spaceship discovered in 1995 based on a puffer engine.

name: R-pentomino
author: John Conway
description: A 5-cell methuselah that evolves chaotically for 1,103 generations before stabilizing.

name: Pi-heptomino
author: John Conway
description: A 7-cell methuselah shaped like the Greek letter pi that settles after 173 generations.

name: Diehard
author: Unknown
description: A 7-cell methuselah that evolves for 130 generations and then vanishes completely.

name: Acorn
author: Charles Corderman
description: A 7-cell methuselah that runs for 5,206 generations and produces 633 cells of ash.

name: Rabbits
author: Andrew Trevorrow
description: A 9-cell methuselah that takes 17,331 generations to stabilize.

name: Lidka
author: Andrzej Okrasinski
description: A long-lived methuselah that evolves for over 29,000 generations before stabilizing.

name: Gosper Glider Gun
author: Bill Gosper
description: The first known finite pattern with unbounded growth, emitting a glider every 30 generations.

name: Bi-gun
author: Bill Gosper
description: A period-46 double-barreled glider gun built from two colliding queen bees.

name: Simkin Glider Gun
author: Michael Simkin
description: A Herschel-based period-120 glider gun discovered in 2015.

name: LWSS Gun
author: Bill Gosper
description: A glider-synthesis gun that continuously produces lightweight spaceships.

name: Switch Engine
author: Charles Corderman
description: An 8-cell diagonal puffer precursor that travels at c/12 and leaves behind trails of blocks or gliders.

name: Puffer 1
author: Bill Gosper
description: The first known puffer train, moving orthogonally at c/2 while leaving behind blinkers and bookends.

name: Noah's Ark
author: Charles Corderman
description: A diagonal puffer made of two switch engines that leaves a diverse menagerie of debris in its wake.

name: 10-cell Infinite Growth
author: Paul Callahan
description: One of the smallest possible infinite-growth patterns, evolving into a block-laying switch engine from just 10 cells.

name: 5x5 Infinite Growth
author: Paul Callahan
description: The unique 13-cell pattern fitting inside a 5x5 bounding box that exhibits infinite growth.

name: Max Spacefiller
author: Tim Coe
description: The smallest known spacefiller, expanding quadratically at c/2 in all directions with zebra-stripe agar.

name: HWSS Gun
author: iNoMed
description: A gliderless gun that continuously produces heavyweight spaceships.
